title: Container mode: worker (bun uid) cannot write bind-mounted /workspace (host uid mismatch) -> EACCES
description: In worker_isolation=container the cam-worker container runs as user bun (uid 1000) but /workspace is a bind mount of the host repo owned by the host user (uid 501 on macOS). bun has no write permission, so workers can READ but not WRITE: the planner composed a valid PRD but `cat > /workspace/scripts/cam/prd.json` failed with EACCES. This blocks ALL workers (prd.json, code edits, git commits) -> CAM-152 container mode is non-functional for real workers as shipped. Fix options: run the container as the host uid/gid (--user $(id -u):$(id -g)) instead of --user bun (must keep claude home/config working for that uid), or make /workspace writable by bun, or another uid-alignment approach. Hard blocker for CAM-139 (autonomous meta-loop needs container). Surfaced in CAM-175 live-validation. Ties CAM-152, CAM-116.

acceptanceCriteria: .devcontainer/Dockerfile declares `ARG HOST_UID` and `ARG HOST_GID` (default 1000) and re-homes the `bun` user to them: usermod -u $HOST_UID bun + groupmod -g $HOST_GID bun (handling gid collisions), followed by `chown -R $HOST_UID:$HOST_GID /home/bun`.

buildDockerBuildArgv (src/supervisor/worker-container.ts) emits `--build-arg HOST_UID=<uid>` and `--build-arg HOST_GID=<gid>`, resolved from the host via id -u / id -g and threaded through the production ensure-up path (makeProductionEnsureContainerFn).

After worker_isolation=container + rebuild, a container worker can WRITE the bind mount: `docker exec cam-worker sh -c "touch /workspace/.cam-write-test && rm /workspace/.cam-write-test"` exits 0 (no EACCES).
The claude config stays writable by the re-homed user: /home/bun/.claude.json and the claude-code-config volume at /home/bun/.claude are owned by the host uid and writable.
Host mode is byte-identical: no --build-arg is emitted when worker_isolation is absent/host; every existing host-mode dispatch path is unchanged.

Quality spine green: bun run typecheck, bun test, bun run check:all (worker-container + ensure-container tests updated for the new build-arg argv, asserted via the pure argv builder + injected fakes, since CI has no Docker).
spec.scope: Align the cam-worker container user uid/gid to the host user at build time so container workers can WRITE the bind-mounted /workspace (fixes the EACCES that blocks all workers, CAM-175 finding). Two edits: (1) .devcontainer/Dockerfile ARG HOST_UID/HOST_GID + usermod/groupmod bun + chown /home/bun; (2) worker-container.ts buildDockerBuildArgv passes --build-arg from id -u/id -g via the ensure-up production path. OUT OF SCOPE: the onboarding/trust seed (CAM-179), the firewall wiring (CAM-176), and any dispatch change beyond the container build/run args.
gotchas: CI runs on macos-latest with NO Docker; ensure-container/worker-container tests inject fake spawnFn/probe and never touch a real daemon. Assert the build-arg wiring through the pure buildDockerBuildArgv argv + injected fakes, NOT a live build.
oven/bun:1.2-slim ships bun at uid 1000; usermod -u does NOT re-own existing files, so it MUST be followed by chown -R $HOST_UID:$HOST_GID /home/bun.
Host gid 20 (macOS staff) may collide with an existing container group; groupmod/assign carefully and verify no conflict (a group with the target gid may already exist).

The claude-code-config named volume initializes with the mount-point ownership at FIRST run. A STALE volume from a prior uid-1000 build keeps old ownership; ensure-up rebuild (docker rm -f container) does NOT recreate the named volume. A one-time `docker volume rm claude-code-config` may be needed on upgrade: handle or document it.

ensure-up triggers a rebuild on Dockerfile mtime change (preflightWorkerContainer image-stale check). A build-arg change with the SAME Dockerfile mtime may not trigger a rebuild: verify the stale/rebuild trigger covers build-arg changes (the Dockerfile edit itself bumps mtime, so the first landing is fine).

Root cause of the EACCES is the uid mismatch, NOT a missing Write tool: subagent-planner writes prd.json via Bash `cat >` and works on host because eduardo owns the files. Once the container user == host uid, all workers (Bash/Edit/git) can write. Do not add a Write tool as a workaround.
Hard precondition for re-running CAM-175 and for CAM-139: validate by re-running the container ceremony after this fix (and CAM-179).
